paper.title: Cleaning up the neighborhood: A full classification for adversarial partial monitoring

settings.name_in_paper: Finite adversarial partial monitoring (upper bounds, known horizon)
unmapped: Loss matrix L in [0,1]^{K x E} and feedback matrix Phi in [F]^{K x E} are known to the learner
Finite outcome set of size E, F feedback symbols
Game-class restrictions (locally / point-locally / globally observable) given per result
settings.definition_quote: A partial monitoring problem $G = (\cL,\Phi)$ is a game between a learner and an adversary over $n$ rounds and is specified by a \textit{loss matrix} $\cL \in [0,1]^{K \times E}$ and a \textit{feedback matrix} $\Phi \in [F]^{K \times E}$ ... At the beginning of the game the learner is given $\cL$ and $\Phi$ and the adversary secretly chooses a sequence of \textit{outcomes} $i_{1:n}$

settings.name_in_paper: Point-locally observable partial monitoring games (anytime upper bound)
unmapped: Loss and feedback matrices known to learner
Game is point-locally observable: all pairs of weak neighbors are pairwise observable
settings.definition_quote: A game is called \emph{point-locally observable} if all pairs of weak neighbors are pairwise observable.

unmapped: Loss and feedback matrices known to learner
Lower bounds proved with stochastic (i.i.d. outcome) adversaries via Yao's principle

conditions: G has no pairs of neighboring actions

source.label: thm:pm:classification
source.quote: The minimax regret of partial monitoring game $G = (\cL, \Phi)$ satisfies R_n^*(G) = 0 if G has no pairs of neighboring actions; \tilde \Theta(\sqrt{n}) if G is locally observable and has neighboring actions; \Theta(n^{2/3}) if G is globally observable, but not locally observable; \Omega(n) otherwise.

results.notes: Trivial games: play the action whose cell is the whole simplex.

conditions: G is locally observable and has neighboring actions

source.label: thm:pm:classification
source.quote: \tilde \Theta(\sqrt{n}), & \text{if } G \text{ is locally observable and has neighboring actions }

results.notes: Minimax regret upper part of the tilde-Theta, achieved by NeighborhoodWatch2 (Theorem 2). Game-dependent constants hidden.

conditions: G is locally observable and has neighboring actions

source.label: thm:pm:classification
source.quote: \tilde \Theta(\sqrt{n}), & \text{if } G \text{ is locally observable and has neighboring actions }

results.notes: Lower bound for easy games attributed to Antos et al. 2013 (ABPS13, Sec 6).

conditions: G is globally observable but not locally observable

source.label: thm:pm:classification
source.quote: \Theta(n^{2/3}), & \text{if } G \text{ is globally observable, but not locally observable }

results.notes: Upper bound attributed to Cesa-Bianchi, Lugosi, Stoltz 2006.

conditions: G is not globally observable (hopeless) and has neighboring actions
results.notes: Hopeless games; not separately proved in this paper.

symbols.C_G: game-dependent constant independent of n and delta

conditions: G is locally observable (with at least one pair of neighboring actions)
tuning: V = max over neighbor pairs of ||v^{ab}||_inf

source.label: thm:pm:easy
source.quote: Suppose \cref{alg:nw2} is run on locally observable $G = (\cL, \Phi)$ with parameters $\delta \in (0,1)$ and $\eta = \frac{1}{V}\sqrt{\log(K/\delta) / (nK)}$ and $\gamma = VK \eta$. Then with probability at least $1 - \delta$ the regret is bounded by $R_n \leq C_G \sqrt{n \log(e/\delta)})$, where $C_G$ is a constant that depends on the game $G$, but not the horizon $n$ or confidence level $\delta$.

results.notes: E in expression is Euler's number.

symbols.K_loc: size of the largest point-local game

tuning: eta_t = min{1/(4KV), (1/(2 V_loc)) sqrt(log(K)/(2 t K_loc))}

source.label: thm:pm
source.quote: Let $G = (\cL, \Phi)$ be point-locally observable, then with appropriately tuned parameters \textsc{RelExp3} satisfies $\limsup_{n\to\infty} \E[R_n] / \sqrt{n} \leq 8\sqrt{2\Kloc (1 + F) (2+F)\log(K)}$. Furthermore, the linear dependence on $F$ is unavoidable.

results.notes: Limsup of E[R_n]/sqrt(n); expression multiplied by sqrt(T). Tuning uses game quantities V, V_loc, K_loc but not n.

conditions: G is globally observable but not locally observable

source.label: thm:pm:hard-lower
source.quote: Let $G = (\cL, \Phi)$ be a globally observable partial monitoring problem with that is not locally observable. Then there exists a constant $c_G > 0$ such that $R^*_n(G) \geq c_G n^{2/3}$.

results.notes: Corrects minor error in Bartok et al. 2014 proof; is_new true as corrected proof, originally due to BFPRS14.

conditions: specific point-locally observable game with K = 2 and E = 2F - 2 outcomes

source.label: thm:pm:F-lower
source.quote: For $n$ sufficiently large the minimax regret of $G$ is at least $R^*_n(G) \geq \frac{F-1}{45} \sqrt{n}$.

results.notes: Shows linear dependence on F in Theorem 3 is unavoidable.
